text: Squawk! Welcome to the living room. She gets home from work at six. It's five o'clock. One hour, no rules.
In the left corner: fifteen thousand years of loyalty and one red bandana. BISCUIT!
In the right corner: nine lives, zero apologies. NOIR!
Round one! Biscuit, the mic is yours.
Yo, check the paperwork: fifteen thousand years deep,
I was guarding their fire while your bloodline was asleep.
I walked out of the forest and I chose to stand guard,
You walked in for the mice and just never left the yard.
I know her by her footsteps, I can smell her bad days,
You know her by the can opener, the only thing you praise.
She calls my name once, I'm there with my tail swinging,
She calls yours twice, you blink, like a phone you leave ringing.
You call it independent? Nah, you're just cold with a brand,
You'd watch her trip and hit the floor, then sit and lick your hand.
They wrote "man's best friend" in every language on Earth,
They wrote "cat" on a litter box. Now tell me what you're worth.
Oof! A litter box! Noir, you good?
Fifteen thousand years, and they still keep you on a leash,
Still spell out V-E-T so you don't panic in the street.
You didn't choose the fire, sweetie. They bred you into a mold,
Took a wolf and made a pug that can't breathe when it's cold.
Me? I wasn't bred, I wasn't built. Darling, I applied,
Walked into their grain stores, cleaned house, and they invited me inside.
You smell her bad days? Cute. You smell the garbage just the same,
You'd lick her tears, then lick the toilet, and you'd never feel the shame.
"Man's best friend" is what they stitch on the collar of the help,
Pavlov rang a bell and you've been drooling on yourself.
She grabs her keys, you're howling like she's never coming back,
I just curl up in her warm spot. That's called trust. Learn that.
Pavlov?! Somebody hand the dog a tissue!
Round two! Biscuit, run it.
Trust? Nah, that's a pretty word for not caring at all,
She could vanish for a week and you'd just stare at the wall.
Pug jokes? Yeah, they bent us. That's on them, not me,
But who walks the blind man safely across the street?
Who's sniffing out the bombs? Who's digging folks out of the rubble?
Who smells the cancer early? I'm the doctor in a muzzle.
Who rode the rocket first? A dog named Laika. That's history.
Cats in space? Please. You can't even get down from a tree.
You knock her glass off the table while you're staring in her eyes,
That ain't mystery, that's a hostage note in disguise.
And everybody knows, if she ever hits the floor,
You'd eat her face by Tuesday. I'd starve right there by the door.
He went for the face! Literally!
You brought up Laika? Sweetheart, you just made my case:
She did everything they asked, and they left her up in space.
That's your whole religion: obey and get betrayed,
Sit, stay, roll over, die, and then they call it brave.
"Doctor in a muzzle"? Dog, you heard yourself say that?
They caged your mouth and called it honor. I got my own door. Cat flap.
I push glasses off the table just to see if physics holds,
You've been chasing your own tail since you were eight weeks old.
In Egypt I had temples. I got buried wrapped in gold.
When I died, the whole house shaved their eyebrows. That's the grief that I was owed.
When you die, they're at the shelter by the weekend, I'm just saying,
"Biscuit Two," same red bandana. Loyal? That's a role you're playing.
Biscuit Two?! That's cold. That's ice cold.
Final round. Make it personal.
Alright. You want personal? Let's talk about March,
When the man packed his boxes and she sat in the dark.
She didn't eat for days, didn't open the blinds,
Who lay across her feet so she'd remember she's alive?
I couldn't fix it. I'm a dog, I don't fix. But I stayed,
Brought her one sock every morning till she laughed again one day.
And where were you? On the bookshelf, judging from above.
You call that independence. I call that scared of love.
I get twelve years, maybe. That's the deal, I know the cost,
So I don't waste a single minute playing cool. That's time lost.
They say you got nine lives, and you spend them all alone.
I got one. I gave it to her. That's what makes a house a home.
Somebody open a window. It is dusty in here.
...Okay. That landed. Give the mutt his applause.
But you only count love when it comes with muddy paws.
In March, I was the weight on her chest at 4 a.m.,
Purring twenty-five hertz. That's the frequency that mends.
You perform it. You need "good boy" like a paycheck every day,
I don't clock in for credit. I'm just there. And then I stay.
You love her 'cause you need her. That's survival. That's a plan.
I could leave through any window. I don't. That's a choice. Understand?
Twelve years? Yeah, I heard you. I'll be here when you're gone,
I'll be the one on her lap when she's crying about the dog.
So keep the "best friend" title. Frame it. Hang it on the wall.
You're the one she shows the world. I'm the one she tells it all.
MIC. DROP.
SHE'S HOME! SHE'S HOME! SHE'S HOOOME!
...I was asleep this whole time.
And the winner? Whoever she pets first. Squawk!
